reviews.text: What the “Machine” filmmakers did here is to point this out in a humorous and lighthearted manner why AI is the last thing humanity needs at the moment. To be sure, it is a cautionary tale and does so without any furrow-browed, tsk-tsk, finger-wagging.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. The Machines puts a new spin on the dysfunctional family trope by setting it in the midst of a smartphone apocalypse.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Rianda and Rowe deliver their smart script with animation that ranges from traditional to chaotic. Even when the presentation jumps around, the film never loses focus.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: PERFECT, Chaotic, Creative, HILARIOUS heartwarming, & the BEST FILM so far of 2021! You’re gonna cry, you’re gonna laugh, & you’ll do both through the entire runtime. I’ve seen the film twice & absolutely adore the film!
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: With a beautiful blend of two animation styles - that may impact the future of this type of movie - Mike Rianda and Jeff Rowe deliver an emotionally resonant story about family, love, and more explicitly, placing ourselves in someone else's shoes.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: It is an animated feature that includes so many cliches, and yet, it is fun and quirky with a burst of visual storytelling about a family that learns to communicate just in time to save the world.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: It's a little patronizing and borders on cliche, but carries a charm and wit that barrel through your concerns with the energy and subtlety of a good old Rick Mitchell Special.
reviews.author: Mark Serrels

reviews.text: In one of the best surprises of the year, the battle between humans and technology is a wild, high-watt blast of comedy and film homages that attaches old and new generations to the love/hate relationship with our phones.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: Director Michael Rianda and producers Lord and Miller have produced the best example of why “the medium is the message”.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines is a fun, family-friendly subversion of “sci-fi disaster” stories with a wholly compelling emotional core and vibrant voice work from the entire ensemble.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: The daddy-daughter dynamic hit me right in my soft spot.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: An inventive, high-energy adventure with a genuine heart that's rarely found in films of its kind.
reviews.author: Cody Dericks

reviews.text: A reflection on the possibilities of the internet and what we've created with it... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: An inclusive family treat.
reviews.author: John Paul King

reviews.text: The feature debut of Mike Rianda, The Mitchells vs The Machines is both a great coming of age film, a fantastic story of a family coming together and learn to be better, and a highly entertaining apocalyptic adventure.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: Frenetic and fast-paced, it's become popular because of a massive marketing campaign.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The animated film The Mitchells vs. the Machines puts a high-energy spin on the over-used apocalypse concept, by balancing heartwarming earnest about family with biting satire about technology obsessions.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: ...an exceedingly slick animated adventure that is, to a progressively distressing degree, dominated by larger-than-life, over-the-top action set-pieces...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Its not just the family that work together, everything seems to mesh perfectly in this joyous and hilarious misadventure. On the surface, theres a lot of gags about our reliance on technology... However, its also about embracing the difference in you.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Not every individual frame of the film will work, but the overall experience carries both enough laughs and hearts to be clearly worth checking out
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. The Machines is the definitive example of an animated feature that is fun for the whole family.
reviews.author: Mat Brunet

reviews.text: Spider-Man changed that and it seems like theyve taken that films success to heart and produced The Mitchells vs. the Machines, which is easily a step above most of its prior content, but may not quite be up to the level they could possibly be.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Mayhem ensues - occasionally too much of it
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Putting the "fun" in "dysfunction" is what The Mitchells vs. The Machines is about, and what family doesn't have some issues?
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: Simply put, I felt more sheer unabashed joy watching The Mitchells vs. The Machines than during any other movie in 2021.
reviews.author: Vinnie Mancuso

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines bounces along on almost frantically funny dialogue and a bippity-boppity soundtrack by Mark Mothersbaugh.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: At once irreverent, spritely, and moving, The Mitchells vs. The Machines skirts the treacly, arch sentiment of 'family-friendly' fare to deliver an animation as profound as it is stylistically audacious.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Of all the animated films this year, the story of an eccentric family stuck at the center of a robot Armageddon, is the funniest and most imaginative of the bunch. Plus, it features a fat pug, so how can you go wrong with that?
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: A delightful confection that takes premises both iffy and old-hat and makes them sing with renewed purpose.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The Terminator-like takeover paired with a zombie apocalypse setting is moderately amusing but far from original or clever.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: [Offers] frenetic pacing, fabulous color, and vivid imagination.
reviews.author: Martha K. Baker

reviews.text: Just like Rick and Katie must find equal footing to parse through the other's very different mindset, kids and parents can use the movie as a springboard towards the same.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: The movie is filled with an imaginative mix of modern and old-fashioned, campy, two-dimensional animation with additional camp references. A lively soundtrack of pop tunes and numerous other funny cultural references spice up the movie.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The weirdness is an affect, but the affection, creativity, and energy of this film are not. One of the best films of 2021.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: First-time feature director Michael Rianda brings together a deeply touching story about familial differences and does so with the renegade spirit that keeps original animation one of our most sacred spaces for unbridled creativity.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: A dynamic family romp, an exploration of parent-child relationships, and an astute takedown of Silicon Valley tech barons, The Mitchells vs. the Machines accomplishes more with its wild, colorful antics than most serious adult films could dream of.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: It's the kind of movie you immediately want to watch again and again.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: With an absurd sense of humour and an inventive visual style, it really flies -- even if it suffers from an under-powered finale and an over-inflated running time.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: This movie is so cute/fun but the script is in dire need of some editing. It is two full hours long and it's so repetitive.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: It's challenging to find a movie that the entire family can enjoy together, but the Netflix movie The Mitchells vs. the Machines is the rare film that could work for everyone.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: A weird and joyful flick, brought to life with the help of the masterminds behind Spider-Man: Into The Spider-Verse.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: Another stellar entry from Sony Pictures Animation that explores the connections between family and technology with heart and humor.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. The Machines emerges as a very welcome surprise within the panorama of contemporary animation and, of course, the Netflix family catalog. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: The film never veers off course. From the start you're immediately engaged by this quirky family, and quickly taken on an exciting adventure. Take in all the gorgeous animation scenery, and enjoy every thrilling stop.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: Sweet with a wonderfully weird edge. Strong script makes it easy for adults to watch with the kids in their life.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: A frenetic, family-friendly romp...
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: Just as the humorous gags work at different levels by accumulation in long pieces and in detail, the visual conception of the film is also like that and it is headbursting in a good way. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: Despite The Mitchells vs. the Machines espousing a rather conservative outlook on the apocalypse ... its coterie of dad jokes and adolescent homages more than makes up for it.
reviews.author: Morris Yang

reviews.text: Whether it's tears of joy or tears of sadness, Mitchells vs the Machines will have you shedding a few of either or both.
reviews.author: Damian Levy

reviews.text: In its celebration of these characters... this film demonstrates how indispensable every single one of us is, and how much those living with disabilities have to offer the world, if only people took the time to notice.
reviews.author: Jodie Hare

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines is an unbeatable combination of humor and heart.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: Just when we think Pixar has dried up the animation creativity well, the Lord/Miller team keeps proving that the genre can be pushed even further.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines deftly interweaves lightly played, relatable family conflict with an overabundance of physical gags, pop culture-inflected jokes, and bright, eye-popping animation.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: It's fun and unconventional, but The Mitchells vs. the Machines ultimately succeeds with the oldest trick in the book: good storytelling.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: A brash, non-stop Energiser Bunny of a film filled with big ideas but an even bigger heart.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: An emotionally moving, funny, visually appealing, and fun road trip movie. Loved the family dynamic and its relatability.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: It's all about family, and worth every moment.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: The use of Maya Rudolph and Danny McBride certainly help straddle the generation gap, and various readings of the film by non-neurotypical viewers have elevated what I dismissed as simply a busy, noisy thing to put children in front of for a while.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Fortunately, the outcome of the robot apocalypse is family bonding for those on screen and wholesome entertainment for viewers.
reviews.author: Hosea Rupprecht

reviews.text: An entertaining and sharp ode to the dysfunctional family, which is nourished by referential humor during a robotic apocalypse. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Del Río

reviews.text: If you're a parent and feel like you've seen the same movies on repeat, have your kids watch The Mitchells vs the Machines. It's now streaming on Netflix and should become their new favorite without annoying you.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Unlike most films in its genre, it gets better as the film gets older. Like most animated tales, it ends with an emotional whopper that will yank at the heartstrings.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Dazzling animation and a heartfelt family story elevates The Mitchells vs. The Machine way above the rest of the animated features out there.
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: Smart, savvy and hilarious.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: There are no jabbering animal sidekicks voiced by standup comics, for example, nor does Katie discover magical powers. Instead, there are good jokes grounded in modern family life, frames packed with visual Easter eggs.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: In "The Mitchells vs. the Machines," family life is a brilliant, ever-changing collage.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: "The Mitchell's vs the Machines" has impressive colorful graphics, it's packed full of endless creative energy, that asks the question, "How are we supposed to communicate with each other if we're all on our phones nonstop?"
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Writer/directors Michael Rianda and Jeff Rowe have answered one of the greatest hypotheticals: what if John Carpenter and "Starship Troopers"-era Paul Verhoeven got the keys to the animation studios responsible for "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-verse"?
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Writers of the hilarious Disney Channel animated series Gravity Falls, directors Rianda and Rowe have crafted one of the most hilarious and heartwarming family films of recent years.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: It has all the well-balanced ingredients that any animated film should include: humor, emotion, action and spectacle. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines is a delightful family film -- an oddball animated road trip comedy with a lot of charm and a little heart.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: The voice casting is terrific, and Coleman is especially funny...
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: 'The Mitchells Vs. The Machines' is achingly wholesome, superiorly energetic and the Furby sequence is one of the funniest things I'll watch all year.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Feels like a carefully manufactured product lacking the mixture of cleverness and heart that would take it to Pixar level...Still, it's more fun than most of today's mediocre animated family fare.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: A dazzling and wildly charming family adventure brimming with creativity and heart. The Mitchells vs. the Machines is bound to be one of the best animated features of 2021.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: The Mitchells Vs. The Machines is a trainwreck from beginning to end... This is the worst film of the year.
reviews.author: Bobby LePire

reviews.text: It succeeds with its own vibe, funny, family-friendly and loaded with positive messages.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Absolutely gorgeous animation and a smart, witty script propel this movie from the opening shot, while the filmmakers maintain a balance of energy and depth right to the genuinely suspenseful finale.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: [Phil Lord and Christopher Miller] continue to develop what seems to be a house style of eccentric, clever, offbeat and positively giddy humor.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: This is a perfect movie for the whole family, which is an all-too-rare thing to find.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines doesn't quite make good on its huge early promise, but it still is a big slice of family-friendly entertainment.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Though it's stuffed with visual gags and outrageously funny set pieces (many involving pet pug Doug), the film never loses sight of its human characters.
reviews.author: Josh Winning

reviews.text: The entire look of the film is as astonishing as it gets, boldly-conceived and perfectly-executed.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Absolutely hilarious and heartwarming, with the most wonderfully zany animation. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: Sony Animation has another hit, with amazing human expression and exciting visuals. At its core it's all about the family, and their flaws that make them beautiful to watch
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: With whip smart humor and electrifying visuals, the latest from animator Michael Rianda notches one of 2021's biggest cinematic triumphs so far.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Nevertheless its writer-directors, Mike Rianda and Jeff Rowe, keep it zipping along. They give us hyperactive - but not overbearing - animation and lots of good jokes.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: This movie knows how to be funny, how to be emotional and how to be pure creativity. (...) You feel it's made out of absolute freedom and love. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jesus Agudo

reviews.text: Take away the serrated satirical edges, and you're still left with a surprisingly delightful story about a dysfunctional family learning how to connect again.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines is a visually stunning, mixed-media collage of a movie.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: The exuberance and passion the team put in really comes off the screen, from the extra flourishes of Katie's "doodle emojis" to the amazing world design.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: Whether through experience or intuition, Rianda and Rowe clearly understand animated comedy from the inside out; the gags stretch and snap as readily as the family tensions.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: The film doesn't lose track of its core thesis, that the family you've got is the only one you'll get.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. The Machines is definitely a classic in the making
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: "The Mitchells Vs. The Machines" provides plenty of laughs while ensuring that you'll never look at your electronics quite the same way again.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines was much more than I expected it to be, a smart, sweet and very funny genre mashup that somehow manages to exceed the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: When I think back on this movie I feel like it could either be like a huge miss or a win and they really were able to bring this together in such a great way... everyone will enjoy it.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: There are so many things to love in TThe Mitchells vs. The Machines. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: This Phil Lord and Chris Miller-produced animated film is a madcap movie-celebrating meta-commentary amusement ride.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: Not only smart, bolstered by strong ideas, but it's consistently fun and consistently funny.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A film of fireworks and razzle dazzle, that pushes the action of loving support for one another to such great heights. I loved it, absolutely.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: A high-spirited shot of energetic eye candy, the movie is also fondly intimate and crude to a T. I loved it.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: Casting Olivia Colman as the voice of a demonic AI is only the first stroke of genius in this sprightly animated movie, produced by Phil Lord and Chris Miller.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: A blast! From the family dynamic to the cool animation, The Mitchells vs. The Machines is such a fun wacky ride. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Impressive work from the co-directors...fine and inventive mix of comedy, sci-fi drama and family road movie.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: A hyperkinetic blast of cartoon color & energy that is also hilarious. Within its tremendous heart beats a family that learns its lessons by being themselves. Rick Mitchell!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: It's hilarious, it's beautifully-rendered, it's genuinely emotional, and it's just a blast from start to finish.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: It's a goofy but entertaining family feature infused with a surprising amount of heart.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: It's a wholesome but off-kilter comedy, with vibrant, creative animation and an appealingly odd sense of humor.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: This movie reaches out to the awkward and the weird... a charming, fun, and wonderful movie.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Combining this tale of epic survival with a family road trip along the lines of "National Lampoon's Vacation (1983)" makes for a genuine "fun for all ages" animation movie. We need it about now.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: A love letter to being different, having a dysfunctional family, and wanting to branch out on your own, The Mitchells vs. The Machines is a movie everyone of any age can relate to and reminisce about.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: Like much of Lord & Miller's catalogue, it's a great example of how a film can be childish whilst still being intelligent and emotionally mature...
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: Pack with hilarious humor and explosive action surrounded by a heartfelt story about family, The Mitchells vs. the Machines doesn't just back it up, it slams the gear shift in reverse and floors the gas.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: If you're looking for a fun film the whole family can get behind, peel them away from their devices and sit them down to watch The Mitchells vs. the Machines.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: An explosion of colors, creativity and unbridled fun. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Can a movie be just too much fun? The Mitchells vs. the Machines is a rambunctious, frantically paced adventure/comedy that makes Saturday morning cartoons of old feel like a documentary about walrus sleep patterns.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines may look like something that's strictly for kids, but there's more here than meets the eye.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Sharp, funny, and self-aware.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: The breakneck pace might be too much for some viewers, but the reasoning behind it is sound. Its wild attitude accompanies heartwarming themes about family, parenthood, and growing up that never get overshadowed for the sake of gags.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Completely off the chain, with eye-popping visuals and genuine heart, it is proof that Sony are now at least level pegging Pixar when it comes to quality animation.
reviews.author: James Hanton

reviews.text: On top of the brilliant animation is a story with a big, quirky heart to match.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines is a rare gem; a quirky comedy with rewarding re-watchability. It draws you in with its high-concept story and witty one liners and leaves you with your heart full and sides aching from laughter.
reviews.author: Burt Peterson

reviews.text: If it doesn't quite have the emotional kick of a Pixar movie it is only because the creative investment has gone elsewhere. Mostly into the hyper-powered pacing.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: The unwaveringly sweet, animated example "The Mitchells vs the Machines," largely avoids the genre's worst cliches for a tear-jerking adventure ripe with apocalyptic fun.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: At times it can't seem to stick to a single story thread for more than a minute. But its emotional design and trajectory are crystal clear, and the chaos feels like part of a grand plan.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Plenty of heart, laughs and action all stirred together into a highly satisfying mix.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines pushes animation to bold new places that truly respects and understands the younger side of its generational divide.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: While the themes are flimsy, The Mitchells vs. the Machines has plenty that's worthwhile.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: A real genre standout, combining a heartwarming family journey with energetic animation and relevant social themes.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Rianda and Rowe impeccably craft unforgettable characters and shape a story told with wit and depth. It's a real treat that you'll want more helpings of.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Through the use of a unique animation style, quirky humor, and on-screen visual gags - there is a lot to love about this dysfunctional family...
reviews.author: Kevin Brackett

reviews.text: When it comes to The Mitchells Vs. The Machines, everyone's a winner.
reviews.author: Matt Maytum

reviews.text: The film's overall aesthetic is a pleasing blend of naturalistic drawings, cartoonier designs and Heavy Metal magazine futurism.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines is a wonderful paean to the best parts of being human, messy emotions and all.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Further proof that producers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller are an animation brand as reliable as Disney or Pixar, and a good deal more likely to provide something that's not only sturdy but genuinely surprising.
reviews.author: Sam Adams

reviews.text: In brief, intriguing flashes, it manages to exude a sensibility that's darker, spikier, and more idiosyncratic than most other animated films you'd plop your kid in front of.
reviews.author: Glen Weldon

reviews.text: It might have a fractious clan at its core but it should make for harmonious, whole family viewing.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: A visually dazzling delight with a heart as big as its ambition, it's a marvellous creation that's entertaining, endearing, and genuinely hilarious.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Stacked with delicious sight gags, absurd one-liners and deliriously silly set-pieces, it's a real watch-it-with-family film, containing enough caffeinated, mixed-media, hyper-frenetic fun to satisfy all but the most jaded of attention spans.
reviews.author: Catherine Bray

reviews.text: "The Mitchells vs. the Machines" not only has laughably eccentric characters but also a script packed with bonkers, fast-paced action - with elaborate, wild visuals to match.
reviews.author: Maya Phillips

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs the Machines is like an encounter with a sentient doodle pad, crammed with ideas that might be the cleverest things anyone's ever thought of, or the most ludicrous, or probably a jumble of both.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: A marvel filled with fun, emotion, and charm. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: This is a hip, vivid, radiant production with relevant themes about technology, togetherness and family.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: [B]y the end, it's [the characters'] fight to stay a family that lingers beyond all the jokes.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Not only exciting and delightful but it acknowledges a crucial truth we usually pretend to ignore: families are weird. Yes, even yours.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Fantastic & funny moments. But terribly unfocused, which is ironic for a movie about someone wanting to go to film school. Rudolph, Bennett, Armisen & Andre do the best work.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. The Machines is a ridiculous, riotous, and relevant adventure fill with great humor and winning sentiment.
reviews.author: Matt Fowler

reviews.text: A real rarity -- a family film that all members of a typical family will be able to enjoy in roughly equal measure.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Fast-paced, funny and filled with great characters, it's one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: It's a high-caliber production from the animation to the screenplay and aces its clever commentary on our overly plugged-in times. Plus the Doug the Pug as Monchi stole my heart.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: 'The Mitchells vs. The Machines' is a zany and sincere mash-up...and the family's surname rocks.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: It is usually not a good idea to go into a movie with expectations. This is the rare case where it lives up to all of them. Stylish, funny, and heartwarming.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Muir

reviews.text: There's a moral at the end (love your family in all its weirdness, or something) and a dollop of sentiment that is contractually required for the genre. But it's the discreetly sharpened edges of "The Mitchells vs. the Machines" that stick with you...
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. The Machines is a colorful and hilarious assault on the senses that functions perfectly as an action movie, family movie, comedy, and audacious exercise in animation.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Believe it or not, there's some finger-wagging and heart-affirming family truthfulness within the zany scribbles.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: A part of me was taken aback by the entire production of The Mitchells vs. The Machines. It's not like most animated films because the visuals are so vibrant and the way it is filmed is similar to live-action narratives.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines doesn't just deliver eye-popping action and big laughs, it's also got a big heart.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: There is nothing artificial about this intelligent, heart-warming and thoroughly enjoyable family adventure, and I can't recommend it enough.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: This is the kind of animated comedy where re-watches are a great benefit thanks to all of the different sight gags and layered jokes that come fast and furious at the viewer.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: A slick, delightfully fun and fast-paced CGI animated movie that sends up the technological crutches that confound our interpersonal relationships.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Laced with Phil Lord and Christopher Miller's signature rapid-fire pacing and colour, it's the goofy-smart and entertaining family fare we've been needing in these fun-challenged times.
reviews.author: Linda Barnard

reviews.text: However you slice it, this is the rare CGI movie that radiates its own kind of inventive beauty, slick without feeling plastic, and the artistry that made it possible deserves to be celebrated on its own merits.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines hits a few bumps in the road along the way, but overcomes that with astonishing visuals, some great gags, and clever social commentary on how technology can affect family life.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: There's something special about those films that can pull you out of a negative spiral, even just for two hours. The Mitchells vs. The Machines is such a film.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: It shouldn't be hard to move on from any negatives scattered throughout Mitchells to find an outing seemingly perfect for the times we live in and a good reminder of the importance of family.
reviews.author: Brian Farvour

reviews.text: The film never drags, the animation is stellar, the entire cast is hilarious and the story does a great job commenting on our obsession with technology and how it has hindered our ability to effectively communicate with one another.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Hilarious and wildly entertaining, The Mitchells vs. The Machines is an absolute gem and one of the few must-sees of 2021 so far.
reviews.author: Adam Patterson

reviews.text: This is one of those special family films that viewers of all ages will find entertaining for different reasons.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: A goofy treat for kids of all ages and a hilarious delight for grown-ups - it's one of the first 'must-see' family movies of 2021
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: "The Mitchells vs. the Machines" offers a nice message about family with eye-popping visuals.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Family Bonds rule over the Machines
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: Funky, a bit peculiar, and ultimately very rewarding.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Bolstered by its ambitious visuals, heartfelt story and sheer imagination, The Mitchells vs. The Machines marks the latest great achievement by Sony Animation.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: Constantly inventive, funny and made with heart, this is likely to be one of the best animated features of the year.
reviews.author: Liam Macleod

reviews.text: Eye-popping, sugar rush chaos that never forgets its intentions regarding healthily navigating the digital age and the importance of not only finding your own people but holding on to something special between outgrown bonds
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: With wildly inventive visuals organically inspired by Katie's filmmaking chops, offbeat humor including an intimidating Furby army led by a freakily giant-sized one and genuinely earned emotion, The Mitchells vs. the Machines is artful entertainment
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: This quirky animated adventure falls into a common trap with its hyperactive visuals, yet beneath the chaotic surface is an amusing and poignant tale of family bonding in the social-media age.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: [T]he most interesting and original animated film from a big studio in years.
reviews.author: Sarah Gorr

reviews.text: I loved this film so much that I immediately bought the art book after watching it. It is such a special movie the whole family will love
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Goofy and colourful and ridiculous and sweet enough for the under-12 set to enjoy, but also smart and witty and self-aware and emotionally complex enough to keep the adults in the room engaged and not infrequently enthralled.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: The Lord and Miller formula requires throwing a lot against the wall to see what sticks. Fortunately more than enough gags do, and we are invested in this fully dimensional family fighting the good fight.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Both a thrilling, giddy family adventure, and the solidification of a radical new visual language in feature animation.
reviews.author: Ben Travis

reviews.text: A fun cross between National Lampoon's Vacation with Will Smith's I, Robot, actually, and yet, it somehow does work
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. the Machines is a charming blend of heartfelt family connection with a wildly fun action comedy twist in its robot apocalypse.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: The cast is excellent, the journey is entertaining, and the underlying messages take it to an entirely new level.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Rianda and Rowe show difficulty sustaining such storytelling velocity, getting lost in the manic energy of the effort, but there are moments of cartoon clarity that keep the movie together.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Stellar animation isn't enough to save this hum-drum family flick from its own bad jokes and bloated runtime.
reviews.author: Caitlin Kennedy

reviews.text: And this The Mitchells vs The Machines review, will point out just how the movie blends outrageous comedy with beautiful storytelling.
reviews.author: Shah Shahid

reviews.text: Has a very high batting average considering the onslaught of punchlines that come at you rat-a-tat from the first frame.
reviews.author: Larry Carroll

reviews.text: Every frame of The Mitchells vs the Machines sings with tremendous attention to detail.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Packed full of boundlessly creative energy, impressive artistry and emotional core...The Mitchells Vs TheMachines will undoubtedly prove a hit with all the family
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: Emotional when it wants to be and hilarious the rest of the time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Adrián Carande

reviews.text: One of the best animated family movies I've seen, The Mitchells vs. the Machines is for the weirdos. Weirdos like me.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: Threaded with clever commentary on our reliance on tech and featuring some incredibly strong design work, this is a pleasant surprise for families looking for something new this season.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: A stylized and unique visual splendor of a film with a heartwarming and hilarious story to boot. This is an animation epic in every sense.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Spirited performances confidently find the humanity and humor in this animated comedy that sends up the familiar rhythms of story, conflict and character while somehow delivering something familiar and fully satisfying.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: "The Mitchells vs. The Machines" is an amusing, heartfelt and often subtle reminder of the limitless boundaries animation can have on screen. Phil Lord and Christopher Miller have done it again.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: For audiences content with rapid-fire juvenilia, the busy patchwork of prefab elements will likely be entertaining enough.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: A subversive delight that should appeal to Gen Y adults and their tech-savvy kiddos alike.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: The cautionary stabs about unregulated big tech that come alongside are no bad thing, nestled within the framework of a brightly coloured kids movie. It's also genuinely funny...
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: When films like these can manage that delicate juggling act of complicated, layered characters, stunning animation, and drop-dead-hilarious gags (get ready to be more terrified of Furbys than you've ever been), we should treasure them.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: The Mitchells is perfect for families, because adults really will enjoy it as much as the kids. It's fun, funny, and incorporates some fantastic action sci-fi sequences.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. The Machines is one trip you'll want to revisit again and again.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs. The Machines manages to deftly move between thoughtful satire, compelling family drama, and painfully hilarious comedy.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: Think of The Mitchells vs. The Machines as Her meets The Terminator in this all new star-studded comedy...
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Absolutely hilarious, as well as heartwarming. The Mitchells are completely relatable and the movie itself is visually stunning!
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: The core of The Mitchells vs. the Machines is its message of the importance of creativity. Sadly there won't be flocks of families getting to see this on the big screen, but maybe watching it at home will make its message resonate even more.
reviews.author: Spencer Perry

reviews.text: While the film certainly lays out the dangers of technology run amok, it also sees its power to connect people.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: Lacking a precise balance of amiable entertainment and intense thrills, the director and producers fail to rein in violent fantasies that spoil what could've been a heartfelt and clever romp exploring family dysfunction.
reviews.author: Erik Nielsen

reviews.text: Colman ... is a scene-stealer each and every time her character (the equivalent of a smartphone) delivers a line.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: As we'll examine within this review, the continuously referential film is structured this way on purpose, encouraging the audience to tap into and examine their own meme culture.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: The Mitchells vs the Machines is creative, hilarious and endearing - and one of the best movies of the year.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

synopsis: Young Katie Mitchell embarks on a road trip with her proud parents, younger brother and beloved dog to start her first year at film school. But their plans to bond as a family soon get interrupted when the world's electronic devices come to life to stage an uprising. With help from two friendly robots, the Mitchells must now come together to save one another -- and the planet -- from the new technological revolution.
